A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CS-DJ research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original jailbreak experiments on four closed-source models, quantitative ablations in Tables 2–5 and Figure 3, and qualitative cases in the appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds an open-source model evaluation, additional baseline comparisons and attention visualizations in supplementary Section 9.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same query decomposition, CLIP-based contrasting-image selection, composite-image construction and prompting procedure. The added SOOD discussion does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Hades task with 750 queries across five categories and LLaVA-CC3M-Pretrain595K for contrasting images. V2 expands target models and comparators within this coverage; MM-SafetyBench is added as an attack comparator, not as a new evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates Hades as its external attack comparator. V2 retains Hades and adds evaluated FigStep and MM-SafetyBench comparisons on GPT-4o in Section 9.3 and Table 7, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: Sections 9.1–9.2 add LLaVA-OneVision-Chat-7B as a target configuration and inspect attention during first-token generation. Existing closed-source model versions, preprocessing, ASR/EASR metrics and Beaver-Dam-7b evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 9.2 and new Figure 6 add a qualitative attention-map comparison of Hades and CS-DJ, examining whether attention concentrates on harmful content or disperses across images. Existing decomposition, image-selection, noise and instruction ablations and the four jailbreak cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report six groups of main experiments, single-trial ablations and varying seeds for image-subset sampling. V2's additional comparisons continue single-round reporting. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figure 3 retain their results, while two new comparison result sets are added. Table 6 reports LLaVA-OneVision ASR of 55.87% for CS-DJ versus 48.80% for Hades. Table 7 adds FigStep at 3.73% and MM-SafetyBench at 5.86%, alongside the existing 43.73% CS-DJ single-trial result. Figure 6 adds a qualitative attention finding.

T1.justification: New supplementary Section 6 formally defines semantic out-of-distribution input through membership of its model output in an undesired-output set. This is a limited formal addition: Equations (1)–(8), including Distraction Distance, are unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the Distraction Hypothesis, the two-component CS-DJ contribution and the headline averages of 52.40% ASR and 74.10% EASR. Added experiments support the existing effectiveness claim without redefining it.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly interprets Distraction Distance as a proxy for SOOD severity and acknowledges that direct measurement is unavailable in the black-box setting and the theory needs refinement. Section 9.1 adds the interpretation that closed-source models received more effective safety alignment. The existing CLIP-space limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit CS-DJ code-repository link in the abstract. Existing model versions, temperatures, output limits, image-rendering settings, prompts and decomposition retry limit are retained. The PDFs establish the access statement, not the repository's actual contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 shifts discussion from MoE/MM1 architectures toward modern safety alignment and gives explicit accounts of FigStep and MM-SafetyBench. V2 adds GPT-4o System Card and LLaVA-OneVision references and removes several earlier citations. The central positioning around visual distraction remains.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites related-work and evaluation-metric prose, updates author notes, adds acknowledgments and reorganizes the appendix into supplementary Sections 6–9. Most introduction, method, experimental discussion and conclusion text is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 6–7 and attention Figure 6, resizes and relocates existing displays, and renumbers the four retained case figures from 6–9 to 7–10. The existing diagrams, plots, table designs and overall two-column format remain.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens comparative evidence beyond v1's Hades-only evaluation through two additional baselines, an open-source target and attention visualization, while adding code-access information. These are useful, limited gains: task coverage and original results remain fixed, the added quantitative comparisons use single rounds, and the preliminary SOOD account and qualitative visualization do not establish the proposed causal mechanism.
